purpose: Prove byte-level binding between multisend_packed_bytes in artifacts and the actual execTransaction calldata submitted to the Safe.

multisend_callonly.note: Absence of 0xf4 in bytecode confirms this is the CallOnly variant — sub-calls with operation=DELEGATECALL are rejected

layer_1_multisend_calldata.description: ABI-encoded multiSend(bytes transactions) calldata. The 'transactions' argument is the multisend_packed_bytes from the test artifact.

layout.note: 32 — dynamic data starts 32 bytes into param head

layer_2_exectransaction.description: ABI-encoded execTransaction calldata. The 'data' parameter contains the Layer 1 multiSend calldata above.

layout.note: 0x140=320 bytes — offset to 'data' dynamic section within ABI body
1 = DELEGATECALL — Safe calls MultiSendCallOnly via DELEGATECALL so it runs in Safe's msg.sender context
multisend_packed_bytes begin here — byte 424 of execTransaction calldata. Offset within multiSend calldata: 424-356=68 bytes = 4(sel)+32(offset)+32(len).
VARIABLE — actual ECDSA/EIP-1271 signatures added at signing time. Length and content depend on Safe signers.

execution_path.step_2: Safe executes DELEGATECALL to MultiSendCallOnly, passing data=multiSend(bytes) ABI calldata
execution_path.step_3: MultiSendCallOnly.multiSend(bytes) runs in Safe's execution context. It reads the packed bytes from calldata.
execution_path.step_4: MultiSendCallOnly iterates: reads op(1 byte), to(20 bytes), value(32 bytes), dataLen(32 bytes), data(dataLen bytes) per sub-call
execution_path.step_5: For each sub-call with operation=0x00: executes CALL to VestingContract with msg.sender=Safe
execution_path.step_6: Sub-calls execute sequentially within the same EVM transaction frame — same block, same block.timestamp
execution_path.step_7: If any sub-call reverts, MultiSendCallOnly propagates the revert, Safe marks transaction failed

sub_call_operation_proof.note: Both sub-calls in both tests use operation=0x00 (CALL), not DELEGATECALL. This is encoded in the first byte of each MultiSend sub-call entry within the packed bytes.
sub_call_operation_proof.verification: First byte of each 121-byte sub-call entry in packed bytes is 0x00. Confirmed by round-trip decode in multisend-encoding-proof.json.

signatures_note: The 'signatures' field of execTransaction is signer-specific (ECDSA or EIP-1271) and is appended at signing time by the Safe UI. It does not affect the multiSend calldata or the packed bytes. The static payload (bytes 0–703 excluding signatures) is fully determined by the artifact packed bytes.
